## Fast and comfortable laser hair removal: power, spot size, optics and cooling systems

HTML source: [Fast and comfortable laser hair removal: power, spot size, optics and cooling systems](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/blog/laser-power-fac-optics-cooling/)

Language: English

Other languages: [Polski](https://ltsmarket.pl/blog/moc-lasera-optyka-fac-chlodzenie-epilacja/), [Русский](https://ltsmarket.pl/ru/blog/moshchnost-lazera-optika-fac-okhlazhdenie/)

> Explore how diode laser power, pulse energy, spot size, FAC optics and cooling influence the efficiency and comfort of laser hair removal.

LTS Market Blog

25.11.2026 · LTS Market

*The future of laser hair removal: technology, effectiveness and safety. Part 4.*

Modern laser hair removal devices increasingly offer high-power handpieces, larger treatment spots, advanced optical systems and efficient cooling technologies.

Manufacturers advertise shorter treatment times, improved client comfort and the ability to accommodate more appointments throughout the working day.

However, a specification of 2,000, 3,000 or even 4,000 W is not sufficient on its own to assess the actual capabilities of a laser.

A diode laser is a complex system in which the radiation source, optics, control electronics, power supply and cooling must operate together.

Only an appropriate combination of these components allows the equipment to realise its potential during everyday professional use.

### What does diode laser power actually mean?

Power, measured in watts, describes the rate at which energy is transferred.

Professional diode laser specifications may refer to several different types of power:

- Electrical power consumed by the equipment.

- Electrical power supplied to the diode module.

- Nominal optical power of the laser diodes.

- Optical power at the handpiece output.

- Instantaneous power during a pulse.

- Average optical power during operation.

These values are not interchangeable.

Some electrical energy supplied to the diode module is converted into laser radiation, while some becomes heat.

Additional losses may occur within the optical system.

Consequently, nominal diode module power does not necessarily correspond to the actual optical power reaching the skin surface.

When comparing equipment, it is important to establish exactly which type of power the manufacturer specifies.

### Watts, joules and fluence

Aesthetic equipment specifications commonly include W, J, J/cm², ms and Hz.

Each describes a different physical parameter.

| Parameter | Unit | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Power | W | Rate of energy transfer |
| Pulse energy | J | Energy delivered in one pulse |
| Fluence | J/cm² | Energy delivered per unit area |
| Pulse duration | ms | Duration of emission |
| Repetition rate | Hz | Number of pulses per second |
| Spot area | cm² | Area covered by an individual pulse |

For constant optical power during a pulse, the relationship between power, energy and time can be expressed as:

E = P × t

Here, E represents energy in joules, P power in watts and t time in seconds.

For example, a hypothetical optical source operating at 2,000 W for 20 ms would deliver 40 J of energy.

If that energy were distributed evenly across 2 cm², the average fluence would be 20 J/cm².

This is a mathematical illustration, not a recommended treatment setting.

Real equipment requires consideration of pulse shape, optical losses, spatial energy distribution and measurement methods.

### Does higher power mean better results?

Higher available optical power may allow a specified amount of energy to be delivered more rapidly or across a larger treatment area.

However, higher power does not automatically guarantee more effective hair removal.

Hair characteristics, skin pigmentation, wavelength, pulse duration and cooling are also important.

The ability to deliver appropriate parameters consistently throughout the procedure is essential.

A laser that achieves high power only temporarily before reducing output because of excessive heating may be less practical than a well-designed system with lower nominal power.

For clinic owners, sustained performance during extended operation matters alongside maximum power.

### Treatment spot size

Spot size describes the area exposed to laser radiation during an individual pulse.

A rectangular spot measuring 10 × 10 mm has an area of 1 cm².

A 10 × 30 mm spot has an area of 3 cm².

At the same fluence, a larger spot requires proportionally more pulse energy.

Increasing the spot area may reduce the number of pulses needed to cover an extensive treatment area.

However, tripling the spot area does not necessarily reduce the actual procedure duration by a factor of three.

Repetition rate, anatomical geometry, operator technique and treatment coverage requirements also influence procedure duration.

Larger handpieces may be particularly practical for extensive areas, while smaller handpieces can facilitate access to areas with more complex anatomy.

### What does research tell us about spot size?

A randomised study published in Annals of Dermatology in 2015 compared two handpieces of an 805 nm diode laser.

The study included ten women and compared axillary hair removal using 10 × 10 mm and 10 × 30 mm spots.

With other investigated parameters held constant, the results three months after three treatment sessions were:

| Spot size | Mean hair reduction |
| --- | --- |
| 10 × 10 mm | 38.7% |
| 10 × 30 mm | 50.1% |

The larger spot was also associated with greater reported pain.

The findings suggest that spot size can influence treatment effectiveness and comfort.

However, the small sample, specific laser system and limited follow-up period prevent direct generalisation to every available device.

A larger spot does not automatically guarantee painless hair removal [1].

### Repetition rate and actual treatment speed

Repetition rate, measured in hertz, describes the number of pulses generated per second.

A repetition rate of 10 Hz corresponds to ten pulses per second.

In a simplified model, average optical power from a sequence of identical pulses can be calculated as:

Pavg = E × f

Here, E represents individual pulse energy and f the repetition rate.

Increasing repetition rate while maintaining pulse energy increases demands on the power supply and cooling system.

Consequently, the maximum repetition rate displayed in the equipment menu may not be available simultaneously with maximum pulse energy and maximum pulse duration.

Operating parameters are interdependent.

Professional equipment should deliver consistent pulse energy throughout repeated emission.

This stability, rather than maximum repetition rate alone, is important for actual equipment productivity.

### Pulse duration and thermal effects

During laser hair removal, light energy absorbed by melanin is converted into heat.

The duration of energy delivery influences the heating of hair structures and surrounding tissue.

An important concept is thermal relaxation time, which characterises how rapidly a heated structure loses heat.

It depends on factors including structure size and tissue thermal properties.

Fine and coarse hairs may have different thermal characteristics.

A very short pulse is not always advantageous. Increasing pulse duration does not automatically guarantee greater safety or effectiveness either.

Parameter selection should account for skin and hair characteristics, equipment capabilities and manufacturer instructions.

A wide parameter adjustment range can therefore be valuable, but appropriate practitioner training remains essential.

### FAC technology: why optics matter as much as diodes

Laser diodes exhibit different beam divergence along two mutually perpendicular axes.

The direction along which radiation diverges more rapidly is called the fast axis.

FAC stands for Fast Axis Collimation.

Specialised optical elements positioned close to the radiation source reduce beam divergence along this axis.

This facilitates subsequent beam shaping and propagation through the optical system.

Potential advantages of well-designed optics include:

- More effective utilisation of radiation emitted by the diodes.

- Reduction of particular optical losses.

- Improved beam shaping.

- Greater control of spatial energy distribution when combined with other optical components.

FAC does not independently increase the energy generated by the laser diodes.

Nor does it automatically guarantee uniform energy distribution across the treatment surface. This requires an appropriately designed complete optical system.

Lens quality, alignment, optical surface cleanliness and mechanical stability are all relevant.

A high-power diode module without appropriate beam management does not necessarily produce high-quality treatment radiation.

### Why do diode lasers require efficient cooling?

During operation, a diode module generates laser radiation and heat.

This heat must be removed to maintain appropriate component operating conditions.

Professional laser platforms have two principal cooling objectives:

1. Cooling the radiation source and equipment components.
2. Cooling the skin surface during treatment.

These are different functions, even when they partly share cooling infrastructure.

Inadequate diode module cooling may result in power limitations, protective shutdowns or accelerated component degradation.

Insufficient contact cooling may affect skin comfort and safety.

Handpiece temperature while the equipment is idle is not sufficient to evaluate cooling performance.

Temperature stability under operating load provides more meaningful information.

### Main methods of skin cooling

Laser equipment uses different technologies to limit heating of the skin surface.

#### Contact cooling

Many diode lasers incorporate a cooled sapphire contact window.

Sapphire has optical and thermal properties that make it suitable for use as a handpiece contact component.

Cooling performance depends on window temperature, skin contact quality and the system's ability to remove heat throughout operation.

#### Air cooling

Cold air systems direct a flow of cooled air towards the treatment area.

They may help limit surface heating and improve client comfort.

#### Cryogen cooling

Certain laser devices use controlled application of a cooling substance in association with laser pulse emission.

Examples can be found in selected alexandrite and Nd:YAG laser systems.

Every cooling method has its own capabilities and limitations.

Cooling quality should not be assessed solely from the minimum temperature advertised by the manufacturer.

### Can laser hair removal be completely painless?

Painless laser hair removal is a common marketing expression.

However, pain perception varies between individuals.

Relevant factors include treatment location, hair density and thickness, pulse parameters, cooling performance and individual sensitivity.

Even an appropriately functioning cooling system cannot eliminate every possibility of discomfort.

Modern technologies may improve comfort, but they should not be presented as guarantees of entirely painless treatment.

Excessive pain or an unusual skin response requires an appropriate practitioner response.

Reduced sensation alone does not establish treatment safety.

### Catalogue specifications versus actual equipment condition

High power, a large treatment spot and efficient cooling are valuable only when equipment maintains its performance throughout its operational life.

Laser performance may be affected by:

- Diode module degradation.

- Optical contamination.

- Contact window damage.

- Restricted coolant flow.

- Contaminated heat exchangers.

- Sensor malfunctions.

- Power supply problems.

Regular technical assessment can help identify these issues.

Independent measurement of actual optical emission using suitable, calibrated measurement instruments is particularly important.

Measurements should account for radiation type, power range, pulse characteristics and conditions applicable to the equipment.

Values displayed on the equipment screen do not replace independent measurement of actual optical output.

### LUMOS as an example of a modern diode platform

An example of equipment representing contemporary diode laser development is [LUMOS](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/new/lumos/), available through LTS Market.

According to the declared product specifications, the platform is available in configurations with stated handpiece power ratings from 2,000 to 4,000 W.

Other declared specifications and technologies include:

- An energy range of 10–240 J.

- A pulse repetition rate of 1–30 Hz.

- Pulse duration starting from 5 ms.

- FAC optical technology.

- ICE Flow cooling.

Catalogue specifications describe the declared capabilities of the equipment. They do not mean that all maximum values are available simultaneously.

Configuration selection should reflect the types of procedures performed and the anticipated workload of the clinic.

### What should you consider before purchasing a professional laser?

Before purchasing equipment, practitioners and clinic owners should establish:

1. Does the declared power refer to the diode module or actual optical handpiece output?
2. Which treatment spot sizes are available?
3. What pulse energy is available for different handpieces?
4. How do operating capabilities change with repetition rate?
5. Does pulse energy remain stable throughout extended operation?
6. How are diode modules and contact surfaces cooled?
7. Are actual optical output measurements available?
8. Which protective systems are incorporated?
9. Are spare parts and professional technical services available?

Answers to these questions can provide considerably more information than a single advertised power figure.

### Conclusion

Professional diode laser development increasingly focuses on productivity, improved energy control and treatment comfort.

High power, larger spot sizes, advanced FAC optics and efficient cooling can all be important elements of a modern laser platform.

Their value, however, depends on the performance of the complete system rather than any isolated technical specification.

At LTS Market, we focus on actual equipment capabilities, technical condition and practical value for professional aesthetic clinics.

Informed equipment selection begins with understanding the technology rather than searching for the largest numbers in manufacturers' catalogues.

### Scientific references

1. Jo SJ, Kim JY, Ban J, Lee Y, Kwon O, Koh W. Efficacy and Safety of Hair Removal with a Long-Pulsed Diode Laser Depending on the Spot Size: A Randomized, Evaluators-Blinded, Left-Right Study. Annals of Dermatology. 2015;27(5):517–522. [https://doi.org/10.5021/ad.2015.27.5.517](https://doi.org/10.5021/ad.2015.27.5.517) [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26512165/](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26512165/)
2. Laser Treatment in Hirsutism: An Update. Scientific review. [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7190465/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7190465/)
3. Laser hair removal: long-term results with a 755 nm alexandrite laser. [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11737124/](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11737124/)

## Multi-wavelength lasers for hair removal: physics, effectiveness and marketing myths

HTML source: [Multi-wavelength lasers for hair removal: physics, effectiveness and marketing myths](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/blog/multi-wavelength-laser-hair-removal/)

Language: English

Other languages: [Polski](https://ltsmarket.pl/blog/lasery-wielofalowe-do-epilacji/), [Русский](https://ltsmarket.pl/ru/blog/mnogovolnovye-lazery-dlya-epilyatsii/)

> Discover how multi-wavelength hair removal lasers work, including wavelength selection, optical power, diode technology and clinical research.

LTS Market Blog

24.11.2026 · LTS Market

The future of laser hair removal: technology, effectiveness and safety. Part 1.

The professional laser hair removal equipment market continues to evolve. While practitioners previously chose primarily between alexandrite, diode and Nd:YAG lasers, platforms incorporating multiple wavelengths are becoming increasingly common.

The most widely used combination includes 755, 808 or 810, and 1064 nm. Some manufacturers extend this range by introducing additional wavelengths, such as 940 nm.

Technological development has also brought numerous marketing claims. Devices are promoted as being capable of removing every hair colour, treating every skin phototype and targeting follicles at different depths.

What actually makes multi-wavelength technology different? Does a greater number of wavelengths necessarily improve effectiveness? Which technical characteristics should professionals consider when purchasing equipment?

### The physics of laser hair removal

In 1983, Rox Anderson and John Parrish introduced the principle of selective photothermolysis, which became the foundation of many modern laser applications in dermatology and aesthetics.

This principle involves the selective absorption of light energy by specific biological structures and its subsequent conversion into heat.

Substances that absorb light are known as chromophores. The principal chromophores in human skin include melanin, haemoglobin and water.

During laser hair removal, the primary optical target is melanin within the hair and pigmented structures of the hair follicle.

Absorbed energy is converted into heat. This heat spreads to adjacent follicular structures, allowing thermal damage to cells involved in hair growth.

The objective is to achieve sufficient thermal effects while minimising damage to surrounding tissues.

The effectiveness of this process depends not only on wavelength but also on fluence, pulse duration, spot size and epidermal cooling.

![Selective photothermolysis](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/multi-wavelength/en/selective-photothermolysis.svg)

Selective photothermolysis

### Why does wavelength matter?

Different wavelengths interact with biological tissues in different ways.

Some are absorbed more strongly by melanin, while others generally have more favourable conditions for penetration into deeper layers of the skin.

However, melanin is present not only in hair but also in the epidermis.

Greater epidermal pigmentation can result in more energy being absorbed by the skin before the radiation reaches the hair follicle.

Consequently, parameters suitable for light skin and dark hair may not be appropriate for darker or recently tanned skin.

#### 755 nm: relatively high melanin absorption

The 755 nm wavelength is traditionally associated with alexandrite lasers.

It exhibits relatively high melanin absorption compared with longer wavelengths commonly used for hair removal.

This can be advantageous when treating pigmented hair, including finer hair that still contains sufficient melanin.

However, stronger melanin absorption also increases the importance of epidermal pigmentation. Appropriate client assessment and parameter selection according to the device instructions are essential.

The 755 nm wavelength does not enable effective removal of hair that is completely devoid of pigment.

#### 808–810 nm: a technological compromise

Diode lasers operating around 808–810 nm have been among the most widely used professional hair removal technologies for many years.

This spectral range provides a combination of relatively good melanin absorption and tissue penetration.

Semiconductor technology enables compact laser modules, high-power diode assemblies and various operating modes.

Modern diode platforms can offer high repetition rates, adjustable pulse durations, large treatment spots and contact cooling.

The engineering flexibility of diode technology has enabled the development of multi-wavelength laser handpieces.

#### 940 nm: an additional spectral range

The 940 nm wavelength is incorporated into certain modern diode laser systems.

Melanin absorption in this range is lower than at shorter wavelengths used for hair removal. The relative contribution of other tissue components to optical absorption also changes.

Research involving combinations of 810, 940 and 1060 nm suggests potential applications in treating fine, less pigmented hair in individuals with darker skin phototypes.

However, there is insufficient evidence to conclude that adding 940 nm automatically improves the effectiveness of every device.

The implementation of this technology within a particular platform is what matters.

#### 1064 nm: favourable conditions for deeper penetration

The 1064 nm wavelength is traditionally associated with neodymium-doped Nd:YAG lasers.

Compared with 755 and 808 nm, it exhibits lower melanin absorption and generally more favourable conditions for penetration into deeper skin layers.

Reduced absorption by epidermal melanin is one reason why long-pulsed Nd:YAG lasers are widely used for hair removal in darker skin phototypes.

Nevertheless, 1064 nm is not universally superior.

Lower melanin absorption may require different pulse characteristics to achieve the necessary thermal effect.

### Does each wavelength reach a fixed depth?

Marketing illustrations frequently depict three wavelengths reaching three distinct levels of hair follicles.

This is a substantial simplification.

Laser radiation does not stop at a specific depth. Its intensity gradually decreases as a result of absorption and scattering within tissues.

Energy distribution is influenced by skin pigmentation, tissue optical properties, water content, blood supply, wavelength and treatment spot size.

Hair follicles are not arranged at three fixed depths either. Their depth varies according to anatomical location, hair characteristics and growth phase.

It is therefore more accurate to discuss relative differences in penetration rather than assigning each wavelength to a fixed layer of the skin.

Multi-wavelength technology also does not eliminate the need for multiple treatment sessions associated with the hair growth cycle.

![Relative light distribution](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/multi-wavelength/en/wavelength-penetration.svg)

Relative light distribution

### What is a multi-wavelength laser?

The fundamental concept of multi-wavelength technology is to combine radiation with different spectral characteristics.

Depending on the device architecture, individual wavelengths may be emitted simultaneously, sequentially or independently.

Several fundamentally different engineering approaches are available.

#### Multi-wavelength diode handpieces

These devices incorporate semiconductor laser diodes designed to generate different wavelengths.

Individual diode groups are combined into a shared laser module. Radiation is then transmitted through an optical system to the working surface of the handpiece.

The most common combination remains 755, 808–810 and 1064 nm.

An important engineering advantage is the ability to incorporate multiple wavelengths within a relatively compact structure.

![Multi-wavelength diode module](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/multi-wavelength/en/multi-wavelength-diode-stack.svg)

Multi-wavelength diode module

#### Platforms with independent laser sources

Another approach involves devices containing separate laser sources.

For example, a platform may incorporate a genuine 755 nm alexandrite laser and a 1064 nm Nd:YAG laser.

Each source has its own active medium and optical characteristics.

Depending on the architecture, practitioners may use the sources separately or select combined operating modes.

#### Hybrid platforms

Certain platforms enable radiation from independent laser sources to be combined while controlling the energy proportions of individual wavelengths.

These solutions provide additional opportunities for personalisation but require appropriate optical engineering, electronics and control systems.

### A triple-wavelength diode laser is not three different laser types

Diode laser specifications frequently contain terms such as Alexandrite 755 nm, Diode 808 nm and Nd:YAG 1064 nm.

However, a laser type is defined not only by its wavelength but also by the active medium in which radiation is generated.

An alexandrite laser uses an alexandrite crystal. An Nd:YAG laser uses a neodymium-doped yttrium aluminium garnet crystal. A diode laser uses a semiconductor structure.

A diode emitting at 755 nm remains a diode laser. A diode emitting at 1064 nm does not become an Nd:YAG laser.

This does not indicate inferior diode technology. It simply describes a different radiation source architecture.

![The source determines the laser type](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/multi-wavelength/en/laser-source-comparison.svg)

The source determines the laser type

### How is power distributed between wavelengths?

Consider two multi-wavelength handpieces with an identical total optical power of 3000 W.

Their spectral power distribution may nevertheless differ substantially.

Handpiece A:

- 755 nm: 600 W.

- 808 nm: 1800 W.

- 1064 nm: 600 W.

Handpiece B:

- 755 nm: 300 W.

- 808 nm: 1500 W.

- 1064 nm: 1200 W.

Both handpieces generate three wavelengths and have identical total optical power. However, their spectral distributions are different.

This is a hypothetical mathematical example, not the specification of an actual device.

In practice, the proportions depend on the number and characteristics of the diodes, their electrical supply and the efficiency of the optical system.

In handpieces without independent control of individual diode groups, these proportions are primarily determined by the module architecture.

Therefore, the number of wavelengths and nominal handpiece power alone cannot provide a complete assessment of device capabilities.

![Optical power distribution](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/multi-wavelength/en/wavelength-power-distribution.svg)

Optical power distribution

### What does clinical research show?

Multi-wavelength technologies have been investigated in clinical studies involving different skin phototypes and anatomical treatment areas.

A 2020 study published in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology investigated the combination of 755, 810 and 1064 nm. The authors reported favourable hair reduction outcomes, although the small sample size limits the generalisability of the results. [[2020]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32484620/)

A 2021 study used digital dermoscopy to assess multi-wavelength hair removal outcomes. Mean hair count reduction reached 75.6% at the three-month follow-up. [[2021]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34418269/)

A 2023 study involving the Soprano Titanium platform included 36 participants with skin phototypes I to VI. Following four treatments and three months of observation, mean hair reduction reached 41.5% in the axillary area and 48.1% in the bikini area. [[2023]](https://doi.org/10.1111/jocd.15674)

In 2024, a study investigated the combination of 810, 940 and 1060 nm in 23 women with skin phototypes IV and V. Mean facial hair reduction reached 66%. [[2024]](https://doi.org/10.1111/jocd.16129)

These findings demonstrate the potential of multi-wavelength technologies. Nevertheless, limitations include small sample sizes, different treatment protocols, varying follow-up periods and the absence of direct control groups in some studies.

These results cannot be used to establish a comparative ranking of individual devices.

![Clinical research results](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/multi-wavelength/en/clinical-research-results.svg)

Clinical research results

### Are multi-wavelength lasers always more effective?

A systematic review published in 2022 included five randomised controlled trials involving 223 participants. [[2022]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35634805/)

Reported ranges of long-term hair reduction were:

| Technology | Long-term hair reduction |
| --- | --- |
| Alexandrite laser | 35–84.25% |
| Diode laser | 32.5–69.2% |
| Nd:YAG laser | 30–73.61% |

Differences in methodology, anatomical treatment areas and participant characteristics make direct comparisons difficult.

There is no basis for claiming that every multi-wavelength platform will outperform every single-wavelength laser.

A well-designed single-wavelength device may provide better results than a multi-wavelength platform with insufficient optical power, unstable emission or inadequate optics.

### Multi-wavelength lasers and light-coloured hair

Hair colour is primarily determined by the presence of eumelanin and pheomelanin.

Changing the wavelength influences how radiation is absorbed but cannot replace a missing chromophore.

White, grey and very weakly pigmented hair remain challenging for laser technologies.

Additional wavelengths may expand device capabilities, but they do not eliminate the physical limitations of selective photothermolysis.

Claims of effective removal of every hair colour should therefore be assessed critically.

### Optical power, optics and operational stability

A laser handpiece is a complex optical and thermal system.

In addition to laser diodes, it contains optical components, cooling systems, temperature sensors and control electronics.

Each component influences device performance.

#### Actual optical power

Electrical device power, nominal diode module power and actual optical power measured at the handpiece output are different parameters.

They should not be treated as interchangeable values.

#### FAC optics

Laser diodes exhibit beam divergence.

Fast Axis Collimation, commonly known as FAC, is an optical technology that reduces divergence along the fast axis of emission.

A properly engineered optical system supports efficient use of laser radiation and beam formation.

#### Treatment spot uniformity

Energy distribution across the working surface is important for treatment predictability.

Non-uniform emission may produce areas with different levels of energy exposure.

#### Cooling

Diode module temperature influences optical performance and component lifespan.

Cooling the skin contact surface and removing heat from the laser module serve different purposes.

The former supports epidermal protection and client comfort. The latter maintains appropriate operating conditions for the laser source.

Both are important for professional equipment operation.

### How to choose a multi-wavelength laser

Before purchasing equipment, professionals should obtain answers to the following questions:

1. What type of laser source does the device use? 2. Which wavelengths does the handpiece actually generate? 3. How is optical power distributed between wavelengths? 4. Can their proportions be controlled independently? 5. What does the advertised power rating represent? 6. What is the actual optical power at the handpiece output? 7. What are the treatment spot dimensions and characteristics? 8. How does the cooling system operate? 9. Are clinical studies available for the specific model? 10. Are professional servicing and spare parts available? 11. Which documents demonstrate compliance with applicable European requirements? 12. Is appropriate operator training provided?

The answers to these questions offer substantially greater practical value than the number of wavelengths listed in a marketing brochure.

### The future of multi-wavelength technology

Further developments in laser hair removal will probably involve not only additional wavelengths but also more precise control over their application.

Independent spectral control, [optical skin analysis](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/blog/artificial-intelligence-in-laser-hair-removal/), digital dermoscopy and temperature monitoring may support the development of more personalised treatments.

Such technologies require appropriate clinical validation. Automation does not replace professional client assessment or operator knowledge.

Intelligent control systems will be the subject of the next article in this series.

### Conclusion

Multi-wavelength lasers represent a natural stage in the development of laser hair removal technology.

Combining different wavelengths has a physical rationale and may expand the capabilities of professional equipment.

However, the number of wavelengths is not an independent indicator of device quality.

Equipment selection should consider actual optical power, laser source architecture, pulse characteristics, optics, cooling and access to technical servicing.

At LTS Market, we believe that professional aesthetic equipment should be selected through an understanding of technology rather than marketing claims alone.

The best laser for your business should meet your actual professional requirements, deliver predictable performance and be supported by appropriate technical services.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Is a triple-wavelength laser always more effective than a single-wavelength laser?

No. Effectiveness also depends on optical power, pulse parameters, optics, cooling and individual skin and hair characteristics.

#### Is a 755 nm diode laser an alexandrite laser?

No. The wavelength may be identical, but the active medium and laser source architecture are different.

#### Can multi-wavelength lasers remove grey hair?

Hair without melanin remains challenging for laser hair removal. Additional wavelengths do not eliminate this limitation.

#### Is handpiece power distributed equally between wavelengths?

Not necessarily. Distribution depends on the laser module architecture and the control of individual diode groups.

### Scientific references

1. [Anderson & Parrish (1983)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/6836297/)
2. [Gan & Graber (2013)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23332016/)

4. [Three wavelengths integrated (online 2021; print 2022)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34418269/)
5. [Systematic review (2022)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35634805/)

## Safe tattoo removal with an Nd:YAG laser: what should you know?

HTML source: [Safe tattoo removal with an Nd:YAG laser: what should you know?](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/blog/safe-tattoo-removal-nd-yag-laser/)

Language: English

Other languages: [Polski](https://ltsmarket.pl/blog/bezpieczne-usuwanie-tatuazu-laser-nd-yag/), [Русский](https://ltsmarket.pl/ru/blog/bezopasnoe-udalenie-tatu-lazer-nd-yag/)

> How does Nd:YAG tattoo removal work? Learn about its benefits, limitations and choosing equipment for a clinic in Poland.

LTS Market Blog

Removing a tattoo calls for a considered choice of method and an individual skin assessment. An Nd:YAG laser can effectively lighten certain pigments, but the device type alone cannot guarantee safety or complete clearance. Here is what to consider before treatment or buying equipment for a clinic in Poland.

![Laser device with a screen and handpieces in a treatment room](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/ndyg-tatoo-article-clean.jpg)

### What is an Nd:YAG laser?

Nd:YAG lasers use a neodymium-doped crystal. Tattoo treatments use very short pulses, including Q-switched systems. The 1064 nm wavelength primarily targets dark pigments; appropriately configured systems also offer 532 nm, used for colours including red. Colours do not respond equally. See [DermNet’s explanation of Nd:YAG technology](https://dermnetnz.org/topics/ndyag-laser-treatment).

### How is the pigment removed?

Laser pulses break pigment into smaller particles, which the body gradually clears. Treatment requires multiple sessions and recovery time between appointments. Session numbers and intervals are individual; complete removal in one visit should not be promised. The [American Academy of Dermatology](https://www.aad.org/public/cosmetic/hair-removal/laser-tattoo-removal) explains this process.

### Safety: benefits and limitations

Treatment can cause pain, skin colour changes, burns, scarring or infection. Complete tattoo removal is not always achievable. A dermatologist’s consultation helps assess the risks. It is misleading to describe every Nd:YAG device as the “safest laser” for everyone. See the [FDA’s tattoo removal information](https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/tattoo-removal-options-and-results) for more on risks.

### Consultation and aftercare

Discuss your health, medicines and tendency to scar before treatment. Afterwards, follow individual aftercare and sun protection instructions. Plan the series around skin recovery rather than a holiday deadline. [AAD guidance](https://www.aad.org/public/cosmetic/hair-removal/laser-tattoo-removal) highlights the importance of assessment and aftercare.

### Choosing equipment for a clinic in Poland

When comparing offers, ask about the specific model’s intended use, wavelengths, pulse type and manufacturer documentation. The name Nd:YAG in an advertisement does not establish whether that configuration suits your planned treatments. Request a Polish-language manual and a device demonstration.

Before buying, clarify training, warranty terms, parts availability and servicing in Poland. For used equipment, request maintenance records and confirmation of handpiece condition. The article photograph is illustrative; it does not establish a particular model’s specifications or availability.

### Costs and service planning

A clinic budget should include equipment, team preparation, treatment-room essentials and a maintenance reserve. Explain the price per session separately from the estimated cost of the series, without guaranteeing a visit count or result.

Compare [new devices](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/nowe.html) and [used equipment](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/uzywane.html), and explore [leasing](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/leasing.html) if you are considering finance. [Ask LTS Market](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/kontakt.html) about options for your planned service. Model availability and suitability need individual confirmation.

## Top 4 Professional Laser Hair Removal Machines in 2026

HTML source: [Top 4 Professional Laser Hair Removal Machines in 2026](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/blog/top-4-laser-hair-removal-machines-2026/)

Language: English

Other languages: [Polski](https://ltsmarket.pl/blog/top-4-lasery-do-epilacji-2026/), [Русский](https://ltsmarket.pl/ru/blog/top-4-lazera-dlya-epilyatsii-2026/)

> Explore Candela GentleLase PRO, LightSheer Duet, Lumos and DEKA Motus AX. Compare professional laser hair removal technologies and features.

LTS Market Blog

24.11.2026 · LTS Market

The modern aesthetic equipment market offers a wide range of platforms designed for laser hair removal. Some use alexandrite technology, while others rely on diode or neodymium lasers. Manufacturers continue to improve optical systems, develop cooling solutions and introduce digital tools that support practitioners in their daily work.

![Comparison of four professional laser hair removal machines in 2026](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/top-4-laser-hair-removal-2026/top-4-laser-hair-removal-2026.webp)

### What makes laser hair removal machines different?

Laser hair removal is based on the principle of selective photothermolysis. Laser radiation is absorbed by melanin and converted into thermal energy, which affects structures within the hair follicle.

However, treatment effectiveness depends on more than the laser type. Pulse parameters, individual skin and hair characteristics, and practitioner training also play important roles.

#### Wavelength

Illustrative diagram of how different laser wavelengths propagate through the skin. It does not represent measured penetration depths or clinical effectiveness.

Professional laser hair removal systems use wavelengths including the following:

| Wavelength | Characteristics |
| --- | --- |
| 755 nm | Relatively high melanin absorption |
| 808–810 nm | A balance between melanin absorption and tissue penetration |
| 940 nm | An additional wavelength used in selected multi-wavelength systems |
| 1064 nm | Lower epidermal melanin absorption and a tendency towards deeper penetration |

Multi-wavelength diode systems expand the technical capabilities of laser equipment. However, the number of wavelengths alone does not guarantee greater treatment effectiveness.

A diode laser emitting at 755 nm should not be confused with an alexandrite laser operating at the same wavelength.

#### Fluence and pulse duration

Fluence, measured in J/cm², describes the amount of energy delivered per unit area of skin.

Pulse duration influences how tissues are heated. Adjustable parameters allow appropriately trained practitioners to adapt treatments to skin phototype, hair thickness and other individual characteristics.

#### Treatment spot size

Treatment spot size influences the speed of treating larger body areas and the precision required when working on smaller areas.

A larger treatment spot may reduce treatment time, while smaller applicators can improve accessibility and precision in more demanding treatment areas.

#### Cooling systems

Cooling is one of the most important components of professional laser hair removal equipment. It helps limit excessive heating of superficial skin layers and reduce treatment discomfort.

Modern manufacturers use cryogen cooling, contact sapphire cooling, air cooling and various combinations of these technologies.

### Top 4 professional laser hair removal machines

Our editorial selection includes four devices representing different technological approaches to professional laser hair removal.

The order of presentation does not constitute a ranking of clinical effectiveness.

#### 1. Candela GentleLase PRO

![Candela GentleLase PRO alexandrite laser](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/top-4-laser-hair-removal-2026/candela-gentlelase-pro.webp)

Candela GentleLase PRO is one of the most recognisable examples of professional alexandrite laser technology.

The device operates at a wavelength of 755 nm, which is characterised by relatively high melanin absorption.

One of its distinctive features is the Dynamic Cooling Device (DCD). The system delivers a controlled amount of cryogen to the skin surface before the laser pulse.

This approach allows skin cooling without the need for contact gel when using the appropriate operating configuration.

Key features:

- Alexandrite laser technology.

- 755 nm wavelength.

- DCD cooling system.

- Multiple treatment spot size options.

GentleLase PRO remains a recognisable example of professional equipment based on established alexandrite laser technology.

#### 2. Lumenis LightSheer Duet

![Lumenis LightSheer Duet diode laser with treatment handpieces](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/top-4-laser-hair-removal-2026/lumenis-lightsheer-duet.webp)

![LightSheer Duet ET and HS handpieces](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/top-4-laser-hair-removal-2026/lumenis-lightsheer-duet-handpieces.webp)

LightSheer Duet is a professional diode laser platform operating at a wavelength of approximately 805 nm.

One of its distinctive features is the use of two different treatment handpieces: ET and HS.

The ET handpiece incorporates ChillTip contact cooling. The HS handpiece uses vacuum-assisted technology and a larger treatment area designed, among other applications, for treating larger body regions.

This approach allows practitioners to select the appropriate handpiece according to the treatment area and their workflow.

Key features:

- Diode laser technology.

- Approximately 805 nm wavelength.

- Two treatment handpieces.

- ChillTip contact cooling in the ET handpiece.

- Vacuum-assisted technology in the HS handpiece.

LightSheer Duet illustrates how handpiece design and energy delivery methods can influence treatment workflow and duration.

#### 3. Lumos

![Lumos professional diode laser](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/lumos/lumos-front-800.webp)

Lumos represents a modern direction in the development of multi-wavelength diode laser systems, combining advanced laser modules, optical technology, cooling systems and digital tools.

The device is available in configurations with a declared handpiece power ranging from 2000 to 4000 W. Its pulse repetition frequency ranges from 1 to 30 Hz, with pulse durations starting at 5 ms.

One of the optical technologies incorporated into Lumos is FAC (Fast Axis Collimation). This technology reduces the divergence of radiation emitted by laser diodes along the fast axis, supporting improved control of the laser beam.

The ICE Flow cooling system helps maintain appropriate thermal conditions during equipment operation.

Another notable feature is the availability of a digital dermatoscope in selected configurations. It allows practitioners to observe the skin surface and hair under magnification and document visible changes throughout a course of treatments.

Key features:

- Multi-wavelength diode laser technology.

- Declared handpiece power from 2000 to 4000 W, depending on configuration.

- Pulse repetition frequency of 1–30 Hz.

- Pulse duration starting at 5 ms.

- FAC optical technology.

- ICE Flow cooling system.

- Digital dermatoscope in selected configurations.

- Professional technical service support in Poland.

Lumos demonstrates a modern approach to professional aesthetic equipment, combining laser technology with additional tools that support practitioners in their daily work.

[Discover Lumos and explore its technical specifications.](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/new/lumos/)

#### 4. DEKA Motus AX Moveo

![DEKA Motus AX alexandrite laser](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/top-4-laser-hair-removal-2026/deka-motus-ax.webp)

![DEKA Motus AX handpiece with sapphire tip](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/blog/top-4-laser-hair-removal-2026/deka-motus-ax-sapphire-handpiece.webp)

Motus AX, developed by the Italian manufacturer DEKA, is an alexandrite laser system operating at a wavelength of 755 nm.

One of its key features is Moveo technology, which uses gradual energy delivery while the handpiece moves across the skin surface.

Rather than relying solely on traditional single-pulse treatment techniques, Moveo technology uses multiple passes to progressively heat the target structures.

A sapphire contact tip supports surface cooling and helps reduce discomfort during treatment.

Key features:

- Alexandrite laser technology.

- 755 nm wavelength.

- Moveo technology.

- Sapphire contact cooling.

- In-motion treatment capability.

Motus AX is an interesting example of how alexandrite laser technology has evolved to accommodate modern hair removal techniques.

### Technology comparison

| Feature | Candela GentleLase PRO | LightSheer Duet | Lumos | DEKA Motus AX |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Laser type | Alexandrite | Diode | Multi-wavelength diode | Alexandrite |
| Cooling | DCD | ChillTip (ET) | ICE Flow | Sapphire contact cooling |
| Distinctive technology | Cryogen | Vacuum-assisted HS | FAC | Moveo |
| Dermatoscope | Not specified | Not specified | Configuration-dependent | Not specified |
| Primary application | Hair removal | Hair removal | Hair removal | Hair removal |

This table describes technological and design differences rather than the results of comparative clinical studies.

Declared handpiece power is not a direct measure of treatment effectiveness. Figures published by different manufacturers may refer to different technical parameters.

### Which laser hair removal machine should you choose?

There is no universal device that represents the best solution for every aesthetic clinic and every client.

Alexandrite systems remain an important part of professional laser hair removal. Diode platforms continue to evolve through improvements in optics, cooling systems, handpiece design and digital technologies.

Very light, grey and white hair may respond poorly to laser hair removal due to its limited melanin content. None of the technologies presented guarantees completely painless treatments or the elimination of adverse reaction risks.

When choosing equipment, business owners should consider not only technical specifications but also operating costs, spare parts availability, warranty conditions and access to professional technical support.

Even the most advanced laser cannot generate revenue while it remains out of service awaiting repairs.

Customers purchasing equipment from LTS Market receive professional technical service support from [Laser Tech Service](https://lasertechservice.pl/) throughout Poland.

## Buying a Used Aesthetic Laser: Why Professional Inspection by Laser Tech Service Matters

HTML source: [Buying a Used Aesthetic Laser: Why Professional Inspection by Laser Tech Service Matters](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/blog/used-aesthetic-laser-inspection/)

Language: English

Other languages: [Polski](https://ltsmarket.pl/blog/zakup-uzywanego-lasera-diagnostyka/), [Русский](https://ltsmarket.pl/ru/blog/pokupka-bu-lazera-diagnostika/)

> Buying a used aesthetic laser? Laser Tech Service offers professional equipment selection and technical assessment for PLN 2,500.

LTS Market Blog

17.11.2026 · LTS Market in cooperation with [Laser Tech Service](https://lasertechservice.pl/)

Purchasing an aesthetic laser is a significant investment for any beauty salon or aesthetic clinic. Whether you are opening a new business or expanding an existing treatment portfolio, choosing the right equipment affects treatment quality, operating costs and client safety.

The second-hand market offers a wide selection of diode lasers, IPL systems, Nd:YAG lasers and other aesthetic devices.

Many of these machines look attractive, and some are offered at prices considerably below the cost of new equipment.

However, appearance alone tells you very little about the actual technical condition of a laser.

**A machine that looks almost new may still contain worn components, hidden defects or expensive technical problems.**

This is why professional inspection before purchasing used aesthetic equipment is so important.

### Why Service Experience Makes a Difference

[Laser Tech Service](https://lasertechservice.pl/en/) specialises in diagnostics, repairs and maintenance of laser and aesthetic equipment throughout Poland.

Our technicians regularly work with devices from different manufacturers, repairing cooling systems, electronic components, laser modules, handpieces and other essential parts.

We understand these machines beyond their product descriptions and marketing specifications.

We know how they are built internally, which components are most vulnerable to wear and what types of failures are common in everyday operation.

**Our experience comes from working directly with the technology, identifying faults and restoring equipment to proper working condition.**

This practical knowledge helps us assess a device from an engineering perspective rather than relying exclusively on the seller's description.

### A Working Laser Is Not Necessarily a Healthy Laser

Imagine finding a used diode laser at an attractive price.

The seller switches it on, demonstrates the touchscreen and shows that the handpiece produces pulses.

Everything appears to work.

But a short demonstration cannot confirm the actual condition of the laser module.

The optical output may be lower than expected. The cooling system may be operating inefficiently. Electronic components may show signs of previous damage or repairs.

A machine can continue operating despite technical problems that may affect its reliability and performance.

Even the pulse counter does not always provide a complete picture of the laser module's actual condition.

This is why professional diagnostics are essential before making a purchase decision.

### What Does Laser Tech Service Inspect?

The inspection process depends on the type and technical design of the equipment.

Depending on the device, our specialists can assess:

- The condition of laser modules and diodes.

- Actual optical output power.

- Handpiece condition and component wear.

- Cooling system performance.

- Pumps, temperature sensors and safety systems.

- Power supplies and electronic components.

- Cooling circuit integrity.

- Available operating and service information.

- Evidence of previous repairs.

- Operational stability and identified faults.

Following the inspection, we prepare a technical report describing the equipment's condition and relevant findings.

This information helps buyers understand the potential risks associated with purchasing a particular device.

### Choosing the Right Equipment for Your Salon

The most expensive laser is not necessarily the best choice for every business.

A suitable device should match the salon's treatment portfolio, client needs, budget and operating requirements.

[Laser Tech Service](https://lasertechservice.pl/en/) helps evaluate equipment based on practical technical considerations.

We consider the machine's construction, serviceability, availability of replacement parts and potential maintenance requirements.

Our goal is to help salon owners make informed purchasing decisions based on the actual characteristics and condition of the equipment.

### How Much Does Professional Equipment Selection Cost?

**The price of the professional equipment selection service provided by [Laser Tech Service](https://lasertechservice.pl/en/) is PLN 2,500.**

This service provides technical expertise that can help reduce the financial risks associated with purchasing used equipment.

Major repairs involving laser modules, cooling systems or electronics can cost considerably more.

Unexpected breakdowns may also lead to cancelled appointments, operational downtime and lost revenue.

A professional assessment before purchase can help identify potential problems before they become the buyer's responsibility.

### Why Seller Assurances Are Not Enough

Not every seller is attempting to hide problems.

Many salon owners sell equipment because they are upgrading their technology, changing services or closing their business.

However, even an honest seller may not know the actual condition of internal components.

Certain faults and performance issues can only be identified through appropriate technical measurements and professional diagnostics.

[Laser Tech Service](https://lasertechservice.pl/en/) evaluates equipment from the perspective of technicians who work with these systems every day.

This provides buyers with valuable information beyond appearance, marketing specifications and verbal assurances.

### Alpha Mini laser hair removal technology

Selective photothermolysis relies on melanin in the hair absorbing light. Pulse energy becomes heat that acts on structures in the hair follicle. The operator selects settings for the skin, hair and treatment area; results and sensations vary between individuals.

Available wavelength variants are 808 nm; 755 + 808 + 1064 nm; and 755 + 808 + 940 + 1064 nm. These are alternative handpiece configurations, rather than switchable features of a single set. The base configuration and options for the offer starting at PLN 40,000 are agreed during consultation.

### ICE Flow cooling system

The system combines contact cooling through a sapphire window, thermoelectric TEC elements, a liquid circuit and air heat dissipation. Skin cooling helps reduce discomfort, while component cooling supports stable laser operation.

The LTS Market product card specifies TEC 500 W. Regular inspection of the cooling circuit, filters and fluid is part of maintenance. Follow the supplied configuration’s manual and adjust the maintenance schedule to usage.

### Handpiece and intelligent features

Handpiece power is 1000–1200 W, depending on configuration. The standard treatment window is 12 × 12 mm; a 12 × 20 mm option can be agreed when ordering. The handpiece has a 2-inch touchscreen.

Handpiece controls allow adjustments to energy, frequency, pulse duration and cooling without reaching for the main panel. The grip supports handling across the treatment area.

Available configurations include Android, CRM for customer and treatment records, error self-checks and software updates. Equipment options also include a dermatoscope with 50–200× magnification and an additional mode for acne-prone skin treatments.

Availability of these functions in your LTS Market set is confirmed before purchase. They are not automatically included as base equipment in the offer starting at PLN 40,000. Applications and settings must follow the device manual.

### Four Wavelengths in One Diode Laser System

Different wavelengths interact with melanin and tissue in different ways. Combining four wavelengths gives trained operators more flexibility when selecting appropriate treatment parameters.

#### 755 nm — High Melanin Absorption

The 755 nm wavelength has relatively high melanin absorption. It may be used in appropriately selected procedures based on skin phototype and hair characteristics.

#### 808 nm — Established Diode Laser Technology

The 808 nm wavelength is widely used in professional diode laser hair removal systems and is commonly associated with reducing unwanted hair growth.

#### 940 nm — Additional Configuration Flexibility

The 940 nm wavelength extends the range of available options in a multi-wavelength system. Its use should follow the manufacturer's treatment protocols.

#### 1064 nm — Different Absorption Characteristics

The 1064 nm wavelength has lower melanin absorption than shorter wavelengths and may be used in appropriately selected procedures, including those involving darker skin phototypes.

Four wavelengths do not eliminate the need for professional client assessment, correct parameter selection or operator training.

### 2000–4000 W Handpiece Options and Flexible Pulse Settings

Lumos is available with handpiece power options ranging from 2000 to 4000 W. Its stated energy range is 10–240 J, with pulse frequencies of 1–30 Hz and pulse durations starting at 5 ms.

These settings provide flexibility within the manufacturer's intended treatment protocols.

Maximum power alone does not determine treatment quality. Pulse duration, spot size, energy delivery, cooling and correct parameter selection are equally important.

### ICE Flow — Advanced Cooling Technology

Cooling plays an important role in diode laser hair removal. Managing temperature supports treatment comfort and helps maintain suitable operating conditions for the handpiece.

Lumos features ICE Flow cooling technology, designed to support temperature management during operation.

Regular maintenance is essential for any professional cooling system. Coolant circulation, system cleanliness and component condition should be monitored according to the manufacturer's recommendations.

Access to qualified technical support is therefore an important consideration when investing in professional laser equipment.

### FAC Technology — Optical Beam Control

FAC stands for Fast Axis Collimation, an optical technique used in diode laser systems to reduce beam divergence along the fast axis.

A properly designed optical system helps shape and direct laser emission through the device's optical path.

Optical quality is one of several important aspects of professional laser construction, alongside diode performance, cooling and electronic control.

### Ray Features

#### Four Interchangeable Tips for Flexible Treatments

Ray features four interchangeable treatment tips.

#### 1200 W Handpiece and 150 J Energy

Ray features a handpiece rated at 1200 W, with stated energy of 150 J at a pulse duration of 200 ms.

#### Ergonomic Handpiece with Touchscreen

Ray combines an ergonomic handpiece design with an integrated touchscreen.

### Four Interchangeable Tips for Flexible Treatments

Ray features four interchangeable treatment tips.

The size and shape of a treatment window influence how the handpiece is positioned and moved across different areas of the body.

Having interchangeable tips allows operators to adapt their working approach to the treatment zone.

The exact dimensions and intended use of each tip should be confirmed in the device documentation.

### 1200 W Handpiece and 150 J Energy

Ray features a handpiece rated at 1200 W, with stated energy of 150 J at a pulse duration of 200 ms.

When choosing a professional diode laser, it is important to consider not only output power but also optics, cooling, energy delivery and handpiece ergonomics.

Treatment parameters must be selected according to the manufacturer's instructions and professional client assessment.

### 12-Bar Diode Stack

Ray uses a diode stack consisting of 12 laser bars.

A laser bar is a semiconductor component containing laser emitters. Multiple bars form part of the light-generating system inside the handpiece.

Correct electrical control, cooling and component condition are essential for proper operation.

The number of laser bars should not be treated as a direct measure of treatment effectiveness.

### FAC Optical Technology

Ray incorporates Fast Axis Collimation, an optical technique used to reduce laser beam divergence along the fast axis.

The optical system helps shape and direct the emission generated by the diode stack.

Maintaining the optical components in suitable condition is an important part of professional equipment care.

### Freon 300 W Cooling

Ray is listed with a cooling system described as Freon 300 W.

The cooling system supports suitable operating conditions for the equipment's components.

Refrigeration systems require correct maintenance, including attention to system integrity, heat exchange and component condition.

The exact refrigerant and cooling-system design should be confirmed in the documentation for the supplied device.

### Ergonomic Handpiece with Touchscreen

Ray combines an ergonomic handpiece design with an integrated touchscreen.

The display provides access to the handpiece control functions supported by the device.

Interchangeable tips help operators adapt the handpiece to different treatment zones.

These features are particularly relevant to clinics performing treatments across various body areas.

### Who Is Ray Designed For?

#### Beauty Salons

For businesses introducing or expanding professional laser hair removal services.

#### Clinics Treating Different Body Areas

For operators who value the flexibility of interchangeable handpiece tips.

#### Specialist Hair Removal Studios

For studios seeking convenient handpiece operation and access to professional technical support.

## Returns, Complaints and Warranty

HTML source: [Returns, Complaints and Warranty](https://ltsmarket.pl/en/returns-and-warranty/)

Language: English

Other languages: [Polski](https://ltsmarket.pl/zwroty-i-reklamacje/), [Русский](https://ltsmarket.pl/ru/vozvrat-i-garantiya/)

> Returns, complaints, repairs and warranty terms for new and used LTS Market equipment. Contact details and how to submit a complaint.

LTS Market supplies new and used aesthetic and cosmetology equipment and provides technical support and warranty service. Below you can find our terms for withdrawal from a contract, complaints, repairs and equipment replacement.

### Equipment Warranty

New equipment sold by LTS Market comes with a 24-month commercial warranty. Used equipment comes with a 6-month commercial warranty.

Every used device undergoes technical diagnostics before sale and is delivered in working condition, as described in its product listing.

The commercial warranty is an additional commitment by the guarantor and does not limit or exclude the consumer's statutory rights relating to goods that do not conform to the contract.

### Withdrawal from a Contract and Returns

Consumers who conclude a distance contract generally have the right to withdraw within 14 days of receiving the goods, without giving a reason, subject to applicable statutory exceptions.

To exercise this right, send an unequivocal withdrawal statement to [sales@ltsmarket.pl](mailto:sales@ltsmarket.pl) before the deadline. Following withdrawal, the goods must be returned or handed over within 14 days of submitting the statement.

Consumers may inspect equipment to the extent necessary to establish its nature, characteristics and functioning. Use beyond what is necessary for this inspection may result in liability for any reduction in the value of the goods under applicable law.

Refunds are processed within statutory deadlines and in accordance with the rules governing original delivery costs and the seller's right to withhold reimbursement until the goods or evidence of their return have been received.

Consumers bear the direct cost of ordinary return shipping where they were properly informed before purchase and the law permits this. For equipment that cannot normally be returned by post due to its nature, information about return costs must be provided before the contract is concluded.

For B2B transactions, LTS Market does not offer voluntary returns of functioning equipment without an individual agreement. This does not affect mandatory statutory rights, including those of sole traders who qualify for consumer-like protection under Polish law.

### Complaints and Warranty Repairs

If equipment develops a fault, please contact LTS Market with purchase details, the device model and a description of the issue.

Under the commercial warranty, the device will undergo technical assessment. If the fault is covered, we will arrange a repair. If repair is not possible, equipment replacement will be considered in accordance with the warranty terms.

Independently of the commercial warranty, consumers retain their statutory rights where goods do not conform to the contract, including remedies involving repair, replacement, price reduction or withdrawal where provided by law.

### Equipment Replacement

Replacement may be provided for a confirmed warranty-covered fault that cannot be effectively repaired, in accordance with the warranty terms.

These provisions do not restrict any statutory right to replacement available under applicable law.

### Damage Not Covered by the Commercial Warranty

The commercial warranty does not cover damage caused by misuse, impact, dropping the device, a broken display, liquid ingress, improper power supply, voltage surges or unauthorised modifications where those circumstances caused the reported fault.

Each case is assessed individually based on the established cause of the failure. Signs of use or external damage do not automatically remove all of the buyer's statutory rights.

### Transport and Delivery of Equipment

Equipment may be sent by courier, delivered in person by prior arrangement, or collected by LTS Market following an agreed collection arrangement.

Equipment receiving address:
LTS Market
ul. Rybacka 7, lok. 203
Wrocław, Poland

Transport arrangements and costs depend on the type of claim and applicable law. For a valid consumer claim concerning goods that do not conform to the contract, the seller bears the legally required costs of bringing the goods into conformity.

### How to Submit a Complaint

Email [sales@ltsmarket.pl](mailto:sales@ltsmarket.pl) with your order number or other proof of purchase, device name and model, a description of the fault and, if available, photographs or video showing the issue.

Phone: [+48 575 254 431](tel:+48575254431).

No specific form is required to submit a complaint. Complaints are handled under applicable law, including statutory deadlines for responding to consumer complaints.

> Alpha Mini – profesjonalny laser diodowy do depilacji. Cena od 40 000 zł. Kup w LTS Market i zyskaj wsparcie serwisowe Laser Tech Service.

Nowy laser diodowy

Kompaktowy laser diodowy do salonów kosmetycznych. Profesjonalna technologia depilacji, zaawansowany system chłodzenia ICE Flow i wsparcie techniczne [Laser Tech Service](https://lasertechservice.pl/).

![Alpha Mini — urządzenie z głowicą i ekranem dotykowym, materiał katalogowy LTS Market](https://ltsmarket.pl/assets/img/nowe/alpha-mini.webp)

### Dlaczego warto wybrać Alpha Mini?

#### Kompaktowa konstrukcja

Niewielki korpus ułatwia zaplanowanie stanowiska zabiegowego, także w salonie z ograniczoną przestrzenią.

#### Profesjonalna technologia diodowa

Dobierz konfigurację głowicy do planowanych zabiegów i sposobu pracy swojego gabinetu.

#### System chłodzenia ICE Flow

Chłodzenie wspiera komfort kontaktu ze skórą i odprowadzanie ciepła podczas pracy urządzenia.

#### Wsparcie serwisowe Laser Tech Service

Po zakupie masz dostęp do zespołu technicznego zajmującego się diagnostyką, konserwacją i naprawą laserów.

### Technologia depilacji laserowej Alpha Mini

Selektywna fototermoliza wykorzystuje pochłanianie światła przez melaninę we włosie. Energia impulsu zamienia się w ciepło oddziałujące na struktury mieszka włosowego. Operator dobiera parametry do skóry, włosów i obszaru zabiegowego; efekty oraz odczucia są indywidualne.

Dostępne warianty długości fal: 808 nm; 755 + 808 + 1064 nm; 755 + 808 + 940 + 1064 nm. Są to alternatywne konfiguracje głowicy, a nie przełączane funkcje jednego zestawu. Wariant bazowy i opcje oferty od 40 000 zł ustalamy podczas konsultacji.

### System chłodzenia ICE Flow

System łączy kontaktowe chłodzenie przez szafirowe okno, elementy termoelektryczne TEC, obieg płynu i odprowadzanie ciepła powietrzem. Chłodzenie skóry pomaga ograniczać dyskomfort, a chłodzenie podzespołów wspiera stabilność pracy lasera.

Karta LTS Market podaje TEC 500 W. Regularna kontrola układu, filtrów i płynu jest częścią obsługi technicznej. Harmonogram ustala się zgodnie z instrukcją dostarczonej konfiguracji i intensywnością użytkowania.

### Głowica i inteligentne funkcje

Moc głowicy wynosi 1000–1200 W, zależnie od konfiguracji. Standardowe okno zabiegowe ma rozmiar 12 × 12 mm; wariant 12 × 20 mm uzgadniamy przy zamówieniu. Głowica jest wyposażona w 2-calowy ekran dotykowy.

Sterowanie na głowicy umożliwia zmianę energii, częstotliwości, czasu impulsu i chłodzenia bez sięgania do głównego panelu. Kształt uchwytu ułatwia prowadzenie głowicy po obszarze zabiegowym.

Dostępne konfiguracje obejmują Android, CRM do ewidencji klientów i historii zabiegów, samokontrolę błędów oraz aktualizacje oprogramowania. Możliwe wyposażenie obejmuje również dermatoskop o powiększeniu 50–200× i dodatkowy tryb do zabiegów na skórze trądzikowej.

Dostępność tych funkcji w zamawianym zestawie LTS Market potwierdzamy przed zakupem. Nie traktujemy ich jako automatycznego wyposażenia bazowego w cenie od 40 000 zł. Zastosowania i parametry pracy muszą odpowiadać instrukcji urządzenia.

### Dla kogo jest Alpha Mini?

#### Nowy salon kosmetyczny

Kompaktowy aparat pozwala zaplanować stanowisko depilacji, a konsultacja pomaga dobrać konfigurację do pierwszych usług.

#### Gabinet kosmetologiczny

Możliwość wyboru głowicy ułatwia dopasowanie urządzenia do zakresu zabiegów. Zaplecze techniczne wspiera jego dalszą eksploatację.

#### Studio depilacji laserowej

Parametry zabiegowe i serwis można omówić przed zakupem, uwzględniając planowane obciążenie stanowiska.

### Alpha — profesjonalne rozwiązanie dla rozwijającego się gabinetu

Wybór lasera diodowego do salonu kosmetycznego nie powinien opierać się wyłącznie na jego maksymalnej mocy. W codziennej pracy równie ważne są ergonomia głowicy, możliwość odpowiedniego ustawienia parametrów, system chłodzenia oraz dostęp do specjalistycznego serwisu.

Alpha to profesjonalny laser diodowy przeznaczony dla gabinetów, które potrzebują wydajnego urządzenia do regularnej pracy. Głowica o mocy 1600–2000 W, okno zabiegowe 12×20 mm oraz chłodzenie TEC 1200 W stanowią podstawę jego konstrukcji.

Urządzenie oferuje również rozwiązania wspierające obsługę zabiegów i organizację pracy salonu, w tym system Android, funkcje CRM, dermatoskop i automatyczny dobór parametrów.

Alpha łączy rozbudowane możliwości techniczne z funkcjami przydatnymi w profesjonalnym gabinecie kosmetologicznym.

### Możliwości Alpha

#### Moc 1600–2000 W i okno zabiegowe 12×20 mm

Alpha jest dostępny w konfiguracjach o mocy głowicy od 1600 do 2000 W. Deklarowana energia wynosi 180–220 J przy czasie impulsu 200 ms, zależnie od wersji urządzenia.

#### Chłodzenie TEC 1200 W — ważny element stabilnej pracy

W profesjonalnym laserze diodowym system chłodzenia odpowiada za utrzymywanie odpowiednich warunków pracy elementów urządzenia.

#### Android, CRM i automatyczny dobór parametrów

Android — nowoczesny interfejs

### Moc 1600–2000 W i okno zabiegowe 12×20 mm

Alpha jest dostępny w konfiguracjach o mocy głowicy od 1600 do 2000 W. Deklarowana energia wynosi 180–220 J przy czasie impulsu 200 ms, zależnie od wersji urządzenia.

Okno zabiegowe o wymiarach 12×20 mm umożliwia pracę na różnych obszarach ciała. Jego powierzchnia wynosi 240 mm², co jest istotnym parametrem przy planowaniu sposobu prowadzenia głowicy podczas zabiegu.

Warto jednak pamiętać, że sama moc lasera nie przesądza o skuteczności procedury. Równie ważne są odpowiedni dobór parametrów, właściwa kwalifikacja klienta i przestrzeganie instrukcji producenta.

### Chłodzenie TEC 1200 W — ważny element stabilnej pracy

W profesjonalnym laserze diodowym system chłodzenia odpowiada za utrzymywanie odpowiednich warunków pracy elementów urządzenia.

Alpha wykorzystuje układ chłodzenia TEC o deklarowanej wydajności 1200 W. Technologia termoelektryczna pozwala kontrolować przepływ ciepła między odpowiednimi elementami układu.

Sprawność chłodzenia ma znaczenie podczas regularnego wykonywania zabiegów. Dlatego tak ważna jest prawidłowa konserwacja urządzenia, kontrola stanu układu chłodzenia i okresowe przeglądy techniczne.

### Technologia FAC — kontrola wiązki laserowej

FAC, czyli Fast Axis Collimation, to rozwiązanie optyczne stosowane w laserach diodowych w celu ograniczania rozbieżności promieniowania w jednej z osi.

Odpowiednio zaprojektowany układ optyczny pomaga kształtować wiązkę i prowadzić ją przez kolejne elementy toru optycznego.

Technologia FAC jest jednym z elementów konstrukcji Alpha, obok głowicy laserowej, systemu chłodzenia i elektroniki sterującej.

### Android, CRM i automatyczny dobór parametrów

#### Android — nowoczesny interfejs

System Android umożliwia obsługę urządzenia za pomocą czytelnego interfejsu, zapewniającego dostęp do dostępnych funkcji i ustawień.

#### CRM — organizacja pracy gabinetu

Funkcje CRM mogą pomagać w przechowywaniu informacji o klientach i historii zabiegów. Dokładny zakres możliwości zależy od wersji oprogramowania.

#### Automatyczny dobór parametrów

Alpha oferuje funkcję wspomagającą wybór ustawień zabiegowych. Automatyczne propozycje parametrów nie zastępują oceny klienta, doświadczenia operatora ani zaleceń producenta.

#### Wbudowany dermatoskop

Dermatoskop może wspierać obserwację skóry i owłosienia w zakresie przewidzianym przez producenta. Nie zastępuje profesjonalnej diagnostyki dermatologicznej.

#### Gabinety z regularnym obłożeniem

Alpha jest propozycją dla salonów, które wykonują zabiegi depilacji laserowej regularnie i potrzebują urządzenia o rozbudowanych parametrach.

**PROFESJONALNY LASER DIODOWY PREMIUM**

Nowoczesny system depilacji laserowej dla wymagających salonów kosmetycznych i gabinetów kosmetologicznych. Cztery długości fal, moc głowicy 2000–4000 W, zaawansowane chłodzenie ICE Flow oraz inteligentne funkcje wspierające codzienną pracę.
